title: RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs
snippet: RFC 9457 (previously RFC 7807) is the standard for Problem Details for HTTP APIs. It defines a common response body format for API errors so clients can read errors in a predictable way. Uses application/problem+json Content-Type with standard fields: type (URI identifying problem type), title (short human-readable summary), status (HTTP status code), detail (specific explanation), and instance (URI identifying specific occurrence).
claim: RFC 9457 is current standard for machine-readable HTTP error responses with type, title, status, detail, instance fields

topic: Error categorization for retry and fallback policies
query: error category classification timeout retry policy budget exceeded
title: Most AI Agent Tool Failures Should Not Be Retried
snippet: Failures can be classified into categories: transient (connection issues, 429 throttling, temporary server failures), contract (invalid request format), authentication, approval, budget-exceeded, state-conflict, and ambiguous-completion. Only transient errors should be retried; others require different handling. Budget-exceeded errors indicate resource ceiling reached and should not retry without human approval.
claim: Error categorization (transient, contract, auth, budget-exceeded, etc.) determines whether retry is safe and appropriate

topic: Error handling patterns for agentic systems

title: AI Error Handling Patterns 2026: Circuit Breakers, Retries & Fallbacks for LLMs
snippet: Standard application error handling answers Did the code fail? through exceptions and status codes with deterministic failures. AI system error handling must answer harder questions: Did the model produce valid output? Did the agent take a safe action? Did the multi-step workflow complete without duplicating side effects? The worst failures in AI systems don't look like failures—they arrive with a 200 status code.
claim: Agentic error handling requires distinguishing structural failures from silent quality degradation in multi-step workflows

topic: Budget exceeded and retry limit error types

title: Are Agent Retry Loops Silently Consuming Your AI Budget?
snippet: A per-run token or cost budget protects against runaway behaviors including loops that do not present as identical retries. If a request has a ten-second user experience budget, three retries of ten seconds each are not resilient—they are a thirty-second outage. Both maximum attempt count and retry budget should be set; workflow stops when either limit is reached.
claim: Budget-exceeded error distinguishes true resource exhaustion from retry-loop amplification; both limits must be enforced

title: Error Handling for AI Agents: A Different Standard Than Classic Apps
snippet: A deterministic error response contract ensures every failure can be programmatically identified without string parsing. This contract must cover both structural failures (network, authentication, resource exhaustion) and behavioral failures (policy refusal, validation failure, state conflict). Every codepath that can fail must produce a typed, machine-readable error with consistent schema.
claim: Deterministic error contract requires every failure to be typed and machine-readable; no string parsing allowed

title: Decomposition section 2.1.6 - Problem type registry
snippet: The platform maintains a closed registry of problem type URIs. Types include: policy-denied, budget-exceeded, idempotency-conflict, cancelled, timeout, partial-result, adapter-unavailable, schema-invalid. Each type carries typed extension members for context. The registry is closed to prevent accumulation of synonymous types across the codebase.
claim: Closed problem-type registry with eight canonical types ensures no string-based error discovery in platform
